verdicts.question: What grade attributes and thresholds do Indian buyers actually use for the intermediate states the platform will list (PET flakes, rPET pellets incl. food-contact status, rHDPE/rPP/rLDPE granules, copper granules, shredded steel, crumb rubber, recycled aggregate, furnace-ready cullet, recovered pulp)? Which standards, and which are enforced in trade versus only on paper?
verdicts.problems: Verification limits first: no web search or page fetch was possible on this machine during the sceptic pass (WebSearch budget spent at 200/200; proxy returns 403 on every CONNECT), so none of the 35 cited sources could be re-found from a snippet. What could be checked was the repo's earlier briefs (docs/plan/research/materials.md, epr.md, sources.md) and the founder's sheet. Findings: (1) The five tyre EPR conversion factors (crumb 1.333, reclaim 1.298, CRMB 0.2, rCB 3.676, pyrolysis oil/char 1.49) are labelled 'prior brief: CPCB guidance document' but no repo brief contains these numbers (grep of docs/ finds none); the CPCB guidance URL exists in sources.md but the figures are unsourced. Treat them as unverified. (2) ISRI paper grade 13 is 'New double-lined kraft corrugated cuttings' (DLK), not double-sorted OCC; only 12 is DS OCC. Not confirmed by snippet, but this is the ISRI Paper Stock guideline numbering. (3) The FSSAI 'EU route' figure 'migration below 10 µg/kg in food simulant' does not match the EFSA criterion (0.1 µg/kg food, or 0.15 µg/kg for adults) and could not be confirmed; the 220 µg/kg surrogate limit is the US FDA challenge-test figure and is plausible. The 23 May 2025 FSSAI guideline date, the four listed decontamination technologies and the authorisation requirement are all unconfirmed by any snippet in this pass. (4) IS 383:2016 recycled-aggregate figures: the 25%/20%/100% RCA caps are consistent with the standard's Table 1 as far as memory goes, but the 'water absorption up to 10% with pre-wetting' figure and the RA limits are not confirmed; the source cited is a Q&A site and a LinkedIn post, not the BIS text. (5) ISRI 210/211 density (50 and 70 lb/ft3) matches the ISRI circular wording (not snippet-confirmed here), and the copper code words (Barley, Berry, Birch, Candy, Cliff, Druid; 96%/94%) match the repo's materials brief, which is snippet-backed; tariff line 7404 00 12 also matches the repo brief. (6) The PET flake numeric bands (IV 0.72–0.78, PVC <30 to <300 ppm, moisture ≤1.5%/<0.5%, hot wash 75–80 °C), rHDPE density 930–970, rPP MFI 8 at Rs 75/kg, and the cullet ppm ranges rest on undated vendor pages (Rekis, 2lians, JB Ecotex, Ribotl, IndiaMART, a Croatian PDF and an Australian report), none Indian-regulatory; they are usable only as editable defaults, which the decision already says. (7) Cat I 40% recycled content for FY2026-27 matches the repo EPR brief (30/40/50/60% ladder from the 2022 PWM amendment). (8) IS 17899 T:2022 as 'Assessment of biodegradability of plastics in varied conditions' is correct to my knowledge but not snippet-confirmed; the BIS draft PCD 21 (21921) title remains open. (9) Against the refined chain: the answer maps to S3 (bales), S4 (flake/regrind/chops/shred), S5–S6 (washed, dried), S7 (pellet/crumb/cullet) correctly, but omits that the founder's refinement puts a compounder (S8) between recycler and manufacturer; for polyolefins the L4 buyer of a compounded, filled or black rPP is the compounder, whose spec (MFI, ash %, filler %) differs from the moulder's, so the schema needs a state field and the 'by-product lot' rule (PP caps/rings, label flakes, fines and wash sludge must be separate lots with a yield on the flake record).
verdicts.correction: Keep the answer's structure and the per-code attribute schema in the decision; change these points. Tyre EPR conversion factors: remove the five numbers until the CPCB guidance PDF (eprtyres.cpcb.gov.in) is opened; keep 'end product type is a lot attribute' since certificates use fixed factors. Paper: ISRI 11 OCC, 12 double-sorted OCC, 13 DLK (new kraft cuttings, a post-industrial grade), 37 sorted office, 54 mixed, 58 sorted clean news; moisture standard 12%; OCC prohibitives 1%, outthrows 5% (not snippet-confirmed). FSSAI food-contact rPET: state only what is settled, namely that FSSAI, not CPCB or BIS, is the gate, that the 18 Jan 2022 direction permitted rPET in food contact, and that an FSSAI authorisation and a Declaration of Compliance are needed; hold the 220 µg/kg and 10 µg/kg figures, the 23 May 2025 date and the four technologies as 'to confirm from fssai.gov.in' and keep the pilot rule 'no food-grade rPET listing'. IS 383:2016: keep RCA 25% plain, 20% RC up to M25, 100% lean below M15 as 'per secondary summaries'; drop the 10% water-absorption figure and RA limits until the BIS text is read. Cullet: keep colour, CSP ppm, metal ppm and size as attributes with no default threshold; the buying furnace's spec is the value. Add a state field (S3–S8) and a compounder buyer (L4) for filled or black polyolefin granules, and make every processing record carry main output, by-product lots (caps/rings, label flakes, fines, sludge) and yield, per the founder's refinement. Status should be needs-pilot-or-counsel for the food-contact and IS 383 items, partly for the rest.

verdicts.question: In the polyester chain, check the founder's technical note (rPET chips melt-spun to PSF with TiO2; are DMT, PTA and MEG used in mechanical rPET fibre production, or only in virgin polymerisation and chemical recycling?), describe the routes Indian PSF makers use, typical rPET share and what a manufacturer wants recorded about an rPET lot; then check the HDPE, LDPE film, PP, paper, ferrous, aluminium, copper, tyre, lead-acid, e-waste, used-oil, glass, C&D, textile and solar-panel chains in the process-chain sheet: what is wrong, missing or out of date, step by step.
verdicts.problems: Verification limits: no web search or fetch was possible in this pass, so no cited source was re-found from a snippet; checks were made against the founder's sheet (refined-roles-material-chains--2-material-process-chains.csv, rows confirmed: PET row 7 lists 'DMT (repolymerisation)', HDPE row 1 'milk-bottle grade', row 4 'IS 4984 for pipes', copper 'ISRI 2400-series', e-waste 'AUTHORISED dismantler (Red 1120/1121)', used oil 'Category I–V', glass '8–40 mm, <25 ppm', C&D 'Orange 1414', lead 'RAINS/RAILS/RAKES', solar 'laminate fluff HW-tagged') and the repo's snippet-backed briefs. What stands: the polyester chemistry (PTA/DMT and MEG are monomers consumed in virgin polymerisation and chemical recycling; mechanical rPSF uses dried flake or pellet, melt filtration, TiO2 masterbatch and spin finish; IV recovery by SSP or chain extenders) is textbook-correct; the ELV Rules 2025 (S.O. 98(E), in force 1 Apr 2025), BWM Rules 2022 (S.O. 3984(E)), tyre Schedule IX (GSR 593(E), 21 Jul 2022), used-oil EPR (GSR 677(E), in force 1 Apr 2024, registered collection agents), e-waste collection limited to registered entities, PV storage until 2034-35, the Rs 22/kg e-waste floor before the Delhi HC, GST reverse charge and 2% TDS from 10 Oct 2024, ISRI aluminium UBC words and 'free lead means rejection', Rains/Rink for batteries, the 296 of 736 pyrolysis plants figure, the Nandini biodegradable pouches from July 2025, the CPCB 2025 Blue-category C&D facility, and the July 2026 CPCB battery handling guideline all match the repo briefs, which were snippet-verified earlier. Problems: (1) 'Recycled-content 40%' for batteries is the BWM 2022 target for 2030-31 (35% applies from 2027-28), so it is not a current figure; 'recovery target 60%' is the automotive/industrial figure for a later year, not the pilot year; both unconfirmed by snippet. (2) ISRI paper grade 13 is DLK (new kraft cuttings), not double-sorted OCC. (3) 'IS 4984 requires virgin compound' and the IS 617/ADC12 'roughly 85% Al' point are plausible but rest on no cited source; the answer itself flags them for BIS text. (4) The Indian rPSF route ranking, '100% recycled input for coarse deniers', and the named plants are explicitly unconfirmed by the researcher; that is honest but means the core 'typical rPET share' question is unanswered. (5) The e-waste category for solar modules: the repo's solar brief records CEEW14, consistent with the answer's 'CEEW group'. (6) The C&D Waste Management Rules 2025 (with EPR from 1 Apr 2026) are real to my knowledge but remain 'to verify' in the repo; the answer says so. (7) Against the refined chain: the answer correctly adds the pre-processor roles (RVSF, retreader, registered collection agent, refurbisher) but does not map each corrected step to the S0–S9 states or say which price level (L3 vs L4) the new roles trade at, nor that residual outputs (acid sludge, spent clay, laminate fluff, CRT glass, de-ink sludge) must be separate residual-waste lots on the processing record with a yield; the founder's model requires that on every processing record. Minor: 'Bengaluru trade splits HM from LD' and 'katran is Bengaluru's biggest textile stream' are unsourced local claims and should be pilot questions.
verdicts.correction: Keep the answer's chain-by-chain corrections, with these changes. Lead-acid: state the BWM 2022 recovery targets as a ladder (automotive/industrial 55% in 2024-25 rising to 60%; portable 70% rising to 90%; EV 70% rising to 90%) and recycled-content as 35% from 2027-28 and 40% from 2030-31, all marked 'from the rules' schedule, to confirm from cpcb.gov.in'. Paper: ISRI 12 is double-sorted OCC and 13 is DLK; drop 'recycled pulp' as a traded state and list bales (S3) with mill-side pulping as an internal step. Polyester: keep the DMT correction; give the rPET share as an open item ('typical share not settled; ask one rPSF technologist'), not as 'at or near 100%'. HDPE and aluminium: keep the IS 4984 virgin-only and IS 617 alloy points as 'to confirm from the BIS text'. Add to every corrected chain the state code of each output (bale S3, flake/chop/shred S4, washed S5, dried S6, pellet/crumb/cullet/ingot S7, compound/alloy S8, product S9), the price level of each hand-off (yard to pre-processor L3; pre-processor or recycler to manufacturer L4), and the residual-waste lots that the processing record must carry (acid sludge and spent clay for re-refining, laminate fluff and CRT glass for e-waste and PV, de-ink sludge and plastic rejects for paper, wash sludge and fines for PET, slag and dross for metals) with a yield. Keep the local Bengaluru trade claims (HM/LD split, katran volume) as pilot questions. Status: partly; the polyester route detail and the battery targets are needs-pilot-or-counsel.
